paragraphs: Net Power is an energy technology and project development company focused on delivering low-carbon gas power solutions. Founded in 2010, our mission is to transform natural gas into the lowest cost form of clean firm power.

Historically, our sole business has been the development of a novel oxy-combustion power generation system (the "Oxy-Combustion Cycle") designed to produce reliable and affordable electricity from natural gas while inherently capturing CO2 and minimizing the production of air pollutants such as SOX, NOX, and other particulates.

The Oxy-Combustion Cycle was first demonstrated at our 50 MWth demonstration facility in La Porte, Texas (the "La Porte Demonstration Facility"), for which construction commenced in 2016 and testing began in 2018. The facility was ultimately synchronized to the Texas grid in the fall of 2021. During 2024, we made significant upgrades to the La Porte Demonstration Facility in preparation for validation testing of commercial-scale turbo expander components. The first of four planned phases of this equipment validation program commenced in late 2024.

In 2023, we began the front-end engineering and design ("FEED") process for our first utility-scale power plant utilizing the Oxy-Combustion Cycle ("SN1") with the intention of locating SN1 in the Permian Basin of West Texas ("Project Permian"). In 2024, we began purchasing initial long-lead materials for SN1. However, after completing FEED in December 2024, the indicative cost estimate at that time was higher than originally anticipated. In response, during the first quarter of 2025, we commenced a post-FEED optimization and value engineering process. In March 2025, we suspended further long-lead equipment releases, but value engineering and certain development work continued into the third quarter of 2025.

During the third quarter of 2025, we completed a market analysis of the Oxy-Combustion Cycle to determine the economic and timing competitiveness of the product. From an economic perspective, the value-engineering efforts on Project Permian identified significant cost reductions, but not to a level that we believed would be economically competitive in the current market on an acceptable timeline. Additionally, given the market's rapid shift in demand for new reliable power generation solutions that can be deployed as soon as possible, irrespective of their environmental impact, we determined it would be challenging for us to develop and commercialize the Oxy-Combustion Cycle on a timely basis to meet this demand and that other prospective solutions that mitigate emissions from gas generation could be deployed sooner and at lower cost than our initial plants. Although we believe the Oxy-Combustion Cycle remains a viable, long-term solution for the delivery of low-carbon intensity power, we also believe that the near-term prioritization of gas turbines with post-combustion carbon capture is the optimal approach to meeting current market demands.

In response to unprecedented demand growth for low-cost, firm power generation solutions with viable pathways to decarbonize, we have broadened the scope of our business to include the development of clean gas power generation using natural gas turbines paired with PCC. Our go-forward business model is to design, develop, build, own and operate clean gas power plants and monetize the products and attributes they generate, principally electricity, captured CO2, and environmental attributes, as applicable. This business model differs from our historical commercialization strategy for the Oxy-Combustion Cycle, which contemplated proving the technology at utility scale and then pursuing broader deployment through licenses, engineering support services, and related fees.

In November 2025, Net Power signed a letter of intent with Entropy Inc. ("Entropy"), a provider of carbon capture technology, to negotiate one or more definitive agreements under which Net Power would, among other things, exclusively license and commercialize Entropy's PCC technology for power generation in the United States and to jointly develop power generation projects. Entropy's proprietary amine-based solvent technology is designed to reduce CO2 emissions from natural gas power plants.

Entropy's carbon capture process leverages solvent process expertise and proprietary waste heat integration intended to improve capture efficiency. We believe Entropy's PCC technology is at a high level of technology readiness and can enable Net Power to develop and deliver clean gas power projects on timelines that better align with current market demand.

We are developing a modular, standardized clean gas power plant product incorporating Entropy's PCC technology (the "Clean Gas Product"). The development of our first project under this strategy is underway and is expected to be located at our Project Permian site in West Texas. Project Permian is now being designed to accommodate up to 1 GW of clean firm power generation capacity and will be developed in multiple phases. Phase I of this project is expected to deliver approximately 80 MW of net power output. As part of securing the equipment for Phase I, on November 12, 2025 we entered into an agreement to purchase two modular gas turbine generator sets ("Gas Turbine Sets"). Final investment decision ("FID") for Phase I is expected in the third quarter of 2026 with targeted commercial operations by early 2029, which would make this project the first operating commercial clean gas power plant in the United States.

In order to allocate capital and resources to this new business opportunity, in the fourth quarter of 2025 we halted SN1 development and testing activities at the La Porte Demonstration Facility. While our near-term strategy is centered on the Clean Gas Product, we continue to believe the Oxy-Combustion Cycle remains a valuable piece of the Company. Our technology portfolio includes intellectual property, engineering capabilities, and operational data from the La Porte Demonstration Facility and related development efforts. We intend to preserve and, where appropriate, enhance the long-term option value of the Oxy-Combustion Cycle, including through continued evaluation of partnerships, additional cost reduction efforts, and monitoring market and policy conditions that could support future commercialization.

We intend to build, own and operate clean gas power plants and monetize the various plant products, principally electricity, CO2, and environmental attributes, as applicable. In addition to selling electricity into wholesale markets on a merchant basis, potential strategic power customers include hyperscalers, data center co-locators, oil and gas exploration and production and midstream companies, and other industrial companies. Potential customers for the captured CO2 may include oil and gas companies and various industrial businesses. Lastly, potential buyers of the environmental attributes are companies looking to reduce their Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, which includes many of the companies in the aforementioned categories.

Net Power's end-markets can be broken down into two general categories: grid-connected and behind-the-meter. The grid-connected end-market consists of selling power to end-use customers via competitive wholesale markets or electric utilities serving end use customers. Our plants are intended to generate power continuously (baseload) and/or as-needed (load-following) depending on commercial arrangements and grid needs in order to complement intermittent renewable power. The behind-the-meter end-market consists of industrial applications, such as direct air capture facilities, steel facilities, chemical plants, and data centers, including those that have significant 24-hour energy needs and desire to utilize low-emission power, which we believe our suite of technologies can provide. Historically, data centers have procured their power directly from the grid, but growing grid constraints across many markets plus growing demand, due in part to the proliferation of artificial intelligence applications, have led data center companies to evaluate co-location of data centers with dedicated power generation facilities.
Key benefits for customers include the following:

•Clean—We are designing our Clean Gas Product to significantly reduce CO2 emissions from natural gas power generation through the integration of PCC and permanent sequestration. We also intend to preserve the long-term option value of our Oxy-Combustion Cycle technology, which, if commercialized, is expected to inherently capture CO2 at even greater percentages while further minimizing air pollutants.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Our Industry
We have incurred significant losses since inception, we anticipate that we will continue to incur losses in the future, and we may not be able to achieve or maintain profitability.
The commercial viability of our power plants is dependent upon the willingness of our customers to pay a premium for clean energy as compared to the price paid for unabated natural gas-fueled power.
We and our partners may be unable to adequately control or accurately predict the costs associated with the development of our projects.
We may be unable to manage our future growth effectively, and such inability could make it difficult to execute our business strategy.
The projects we are developing will rely on complex machinery for their operation, and deployment involves a significant degree of risk and uncertainty in terms of operational performance and costs.

If we, our partners or our third-party suppliers experience any delays in the development and manufacturing of key components of our power plants, our business and financial condition may be adversely impacted.
We may pursue the development of Net Power plants through joint ventures, which may lead to disagreements with our joint venture partners and adversely affect our interest in the joint ventures.
Lack of availability or increased costs of component raw materials may affect manufacturing processes for plant equipment and increase our overall costs.
Manufacturing and transportation of key equipment may be dependent on open global supply chains. Supply chain issues could negatively impact deployment schedules.

Risks Related to Government Regulation
We must obtain regulatory approvals and permits before we construct power plants, and approvals may be denied or delayed.

We may encounter substantial delays in the design, manufacture, regulatory approval and launch of power plants, and that could prevent us from commercializing and deploying our power plants on a timely basis, if at all.

We are subject to environmental, health, and safety laws and to regulations including, if applicable, remediation matters that could adversely affect our business, results of operation and reputation.

Transition risks related to climate change, including negative shifts in investor, regulator, and broader public sentiment with respect to fossil fuels, could have a material and adverse effects on us.
Restrictions on the ability to procure natural gas, including its production and delivery, and the ability to construct carbon sequestration facilities, could adversely impact our business.
We are exposed to price volatility risks related to incentives.
Any potential changes or reductions in available government incentives promoting projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions may adversely affect our ability to grow our business.

paragraphs: The section below discusses the most significant risk factors that may materially adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Net Power has historically incurred significant losses and experienced negative cash flows since inception, including net losses of $578.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 and $49.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. We have not generated any material revenue, but we have substantial overhead

expenses. We do not expect to generate meaningful revenue unless and until we are able to complete our first commercial plant deployment, and we may not be able to accomplish this milestone on our anticipated timetable, if at all. We have not yet commercialized our products and may never do so successfully, and, as a result, it is difficult for us to predict our future operating results. Our losses may be larger than anticipated, and we may not achieve profitability according to our expected timeline or at all; even if we do, we may not be able to maintain or increase profitability.

Although we expect our operating expenses to decrease over the next several years as compared to prior years as a result of the suspension of testing efforts at our La Porte Demonstration Facility and the change in the focus of our business to PCC, we still expect our operating expenses to significantly outpace our revenue in the short term. Any failure to increase our revenue sufficiently over time to keep pace with our expenses could prevent us from achieving or maintaining profitability or positive cash flow. Furthermore, if our future growth and operating performance fail to meet investor or analyst expectations, or if we have future negative cash flows or losses resulting from our investment in acquiring customers or expanding our operations, this could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial condition.

We recently broadened the scope of our business, and we may not be able to successfully execute on our broadened business strategy in a cost-effective manner. If we fail to execute on our broadened business strategy, for whatever reason, it could materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations.

In response to recent adverse events that ultimately resulted in the Company recognizing an impairment loss, we broadened the scope of our business to also include the generation of power using more standard simple cycle and combined cycle natural gas turbines in combination with PCC technology as a means of capturing the CO2 generated by those turbines. If we are unable to successfully execute on our broadened business strategy, which includes, among other things, developing additional technologies and generating customer interest in any resulting products, our business and results of operations could be adversely affected.

paragraphs: The following management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") provides information that management believes is relevant to an assessment and understanding of our consolidated results of operations and financial condition and includes forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. This section should be read in conjunction with Part I of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Part II Item 8 in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and the section titled "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" included in the forepart in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this section to "Net Power," "we," "us," or "our" and the "Company" refer to the business of Net Power Inc. and its subsidiaries. Additional terms used herein are defined in the section entitled "Certain Defined Terms" and elsewhere in this Report.

We are an energy technology and project development company focused on delivering low-carbon gas power solutions. Historically, our sole business has been the development of a novel oxy-combustion power generation system designed to produce reliable and affordable electricity from natural gas while capturing virtually all atmospheric emissions (the "Oxy-Combustion Cycle"). Recently, we have broadened the scope of our business to include the generation of power using natural gas turbines paired with PCC technology that we intend to license from Entropy.

We believe that our performance and future success depend on a number of factors that present significant opportunities for us but also pose risks and challenges, including, but not limited to, our ability to license PCC technology from Entropy, potential supply chain issues, changes in tax policies and other incentives supporting carbon capture, our access to the capital needed to finance the development of our projects, and development of competing energy technologies sooner or at a lesser cost than our products. Supply chain issues related to the manufacturing and transportation of key equipment, including as a result of tariffs imposed by the U.S. or other countries or other trade barriers, measures, or conflicts, may lead to a delay in our commercialization efforts, which could impact our results of operations, financial condition and prospects. Also, currency fluctuations, inflation, and tariffs and other trade barriers, measures or conflicts may significantly increase freight charges, raw material costs and other expenses associated with our business, and such increased costs could materially and adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition and prospects.

Net Power is progressing its first clean firm power hub at the Project Permian site in West Texas. The project is being sized to accommodate up to one gigawatt of clean firm power generation capacity. We intend for Phase I of the project to utilize readily available gas turbines paired with Entropy's PCC technology. On November 12, 2025, we entered into an agreement to purchase two modular gas turbine generator sets with nominal gross power of approximately 30 megawatts each for use at Project Permian. Final investment decision ("FID") for Phase I is expected in the third quarter of 2026 with targeted commercial operations by early 2029, which would make it the first commercial clean gas power project in the United States.

We are a development stage company and our historical results may not be indicative of our future results, particularly considering the recent shift in the anticipated timing of our technology development of the Oxy-Combustion Cycle and the introduction of the Clean Gas Product. Accordingly, the drivers of our future financial results, as well as the components of such results, may not be comparable to our historical or future results of operations.

paragraphs: Net Power 是一家能源科技與專案開發公司，專注於提供低碳氣體發電解決方案。成立於 2010 年，我們的使命是將天然氣轉化為成本最低的潔淨穩定電力。
歷來，我們唯一的業務為開發一種新型氧燃燒發電系統（"Oxy-Combustion Cycle"），設計用以從天然氣產生可靠且經濟的電力，同時內建捕獲 CO2 並減少空氣污染物如 SOX、NOX 及其他顆粒物的產生。

Oxy-Combustion Cycle 首次在位於德克薩斯州拉波特（La Porte, Texas）的 50 MWth 示範設施（"La Porte 示範設施"）中進行演示，該設施於 2016 年開始建設，2018 年開始測試。該設施最終於 2021 年秋季與德克薩斯州電網同步。在 2024 年，我們對 La Porte 示範設施進行了重大升級，以準備商業規模渦輪膨脹零組件的驗證測試。此設備驗證計畫的四個預計階段中，第一階段於 2024 年年底開始。

在 2023 年，我們開始進行第一座電力廠（"SN1"）的前端工程與設計（"FEED"）程序，該電力廠採用 Oxy-Combustion Cycle，並有意將 SN1 設置於德克薩斯州西部的 Permian 盆地（"Project Permian"）。在 2024 年，我們開始購買 SN1 的初始長週期材料。然而，在 2024 年 12 月完成 FEED 後，當時的預估成本高於原先預期。為此，我們於 2025 年第一季啟動了 FEED 後的優化與價值工程程序。在 2025 年 3 月，我們暫停進一步的長週期設備發貨，但價值工程與某些開發工作持續至 2025 年第三季。

在 2025 年第三季，我們完成對 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 的市場分析，以評估該產品的經濟與時間競爭力。從經濟觀點來看，Project Permian 的價值工程努力識別出顯著的成本降低，但未達到我們認為在目前市場上可接受時間內具經濟競爭力的水平。此外，考慮到市場對新可靠電力發電解決方案的需求快速轉變，這些解決方案可盡快部署，不論其環境影響，我們認為要開發並商業化 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 以符合此需求，時間上將具有挑戰性，且其他預期可減少天然氣發電排放的解決方案可能能更快且成本更低地部署。儘管我們認為 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 儘管仍是長期提供低碳強度電力的可行解決方案，但我們也認為，目前市場需求的優先考量應為搭配後燃碳捕獲的天然氣渦輪機。

為回應對低成本、穩定電力發電解決方案的空前需求增長，並具備可行的減碳路徑，我們已擴展業務範疇，包括開發使用天然氣渦輪機搭配 PCC 的潔淨氣體發電。我們的未來業務模式為設計、開發、建設、擁有並營運潔淨氣體發電廠，並透過其產生的產品與屬性（主要是電力、捕獲的 CO2 及環境屬性）進行商業化。此業務模式與我們過去對 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 的商業化策略不同，過去的策略是證明該技術在電力公司規模的應用，然後透過授權、工程支援服務及相關費用進行廣泛部署。

2025 年 11 月，Net Power 與 Entropy Inc.（"Entropy"）簽訂意向書，Entropy 是一家提供碳捕獲技術的公司，雙方將協議 negotiate 一個或多個最終協議，Net Power 將在其中，除了其他事項外，獨家授權與商業化 Entropy 的 PCC 技術用於美國的電力發電，並共同開發電力發電專案。Entropy 的專利胺基溶劑技術設計用以減少天然氣發電廠的 CO2 排放。
Entropy 的碳捕獲過程利用溶劑工藝專業知識與專利廢熱整合，旨在提高捕獲效率。我們認為 Entropy 的 PCC 技術已達到較高的技術準備階段，並能讓 Net Power 開發與交付潔淨氣體發電專案，其時間表更符合目前市場需求。

我們正在開發一種模組化、標準化的潔淨氣體發電廠產品，整合 Entropy 的 PCC 技術（稱為「潔淨氣體產品」）。我們根據此策略的第一個專案開發工作已經展開，預期將位於德克薩斯州西部的 Project Permian 站點。Project Permian 現在正在設計中，以容納最高達 1 GW 的潔淨穩定發電容量，並將分階段進行開發。此專案的第一階段預期將提供約 80 MW 的淨發電量。作為取得第一階段設備的其中一環，我們於 2025 年 11 月 12 日簽訂協議，購買新型模組化天然氣渦輪發電機組（「天然氣渦輪機組」）。第一階段的最終投資決策（「FID」）預期於 2026 年第三季做出，目標商業運作時間為 2029 年初，這將使此專案成為美國首座營運中的商業潔淨氣體發電廠。

為將資金與資源分配至此新業務機會，我們於 2025 年第四季中止 SN1 的開發與測試活動於 La Porte 示範設施。雖然我們的短期策略以潔淨氣體產品為中心，我們仍相信 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 為本公司的重要技術之一。我們的技術組合包括來自 La Porte 示範設施及相關開發工作的智慧財產權、工程能力與運營數據。我們有意圖維護並在適當情況下提升 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 技術的長期選擇價值，包括透過持續評估合作夥伴關係、額外的成本降低努力，以及監測可能支持未來商業化的市場與政策條件。

我們有意圖建設、擁有並營運潔淨氣體發電廠，並透過各種發電廠產品進行資產化，主要為電力、CO2 以及環境屬性（視情況而定）。除了以商業模式將電力銷售至電力交易市場外，潛在的戰略電力客戶包括超大型資料中心、資料中心共置服務商、油氣勘探與生產及中游公司，以及其他工業公司。潛在的 CO2 捕獲客戶可能包括油氣公司及各種工業企業。最後，潛在的環境屬性買家為希望減少其 Scope 2 綠house gas 排放的公司，包括許多前述類別中的公司。

Net Power 的最終市場可分為兩大類別：連網市場與後端市場。連網市場為透過競爭性電力交易市場或電力公司服務最終用戶，將電力銷售給最終用戶。我們的發電廠旨在持續發電（基載）及/或按需發電（負載追蹤），視商業協議及電網需求而定，以補充間歇性可再生能源。後端市場則為工業應用，例如直接空氣捕獲設施、鋼鐵廠、化學廠及資料中心，包括那些有顯著 24 小時能源需求且希望使用低排放電力的設施，我們相信我們的技術組合可提供此類服務。歷來，資料中心會直接從電網購電，但許多市場的電網限制日益嚴峻，加上因人工智慧應用的普及而導致的電力需求增加，已使資料中心公司評估將資料中心與專用電力發電設施共置。
客戶的主要優勢如下：
•潔淨—我們設計潔淨氣體產品，透過整合 PCC 與永久封存技術，大幅降低天然氣發電的 CO2 排放。我們也意圖維護本公司 Oxy-Combustion Cycle 技術的長期選擇價值，若該技術商業化，預期將能更有效地捕獲 CO2，同時進一步減少空氣污染物。

paragraphs: 下列管理層討論與分析（"MD&A"）提供資訊，管理層認為此資訊與評估及瞭解我們合併營運成果與財務狀況相關，並包含涉及風險、不確定性與假設的展望性陳述。本節應與本年度10-K申報表第一部分、本年度10-K申報表第二部分第8項所包含的合併財務報表及相關附註，以及本年度10-K申報表前半部分所包含的"展望性陳述警示"節合併閱讀。
除非文意另有明確說明，本節所有提及"Net Power"、"我們"、"我們"或"我們的"及"本公司"之參考，均指Net Power Inc.及其子公司之業務。本節所使用之其他術語，其定義於"特定定義術語"節及其他處於本報告中。
我們是一家專注於提供低碳氣體發電解決方案的能源科技與項目開發公司。歷來，我們唯一業務為開發一種新型氧燃燒發電系統，用以從天然氣產生可靠且經濟的電力，同時幾乎完全捕獲大氣排放（"氧燃燒循環"）。近期，我們已擴展業務範疇，包括使用天然氣渦輪機搭配PCC技術產生電力，我們有意從Entropy取得此技術的授權。

我們相信，我們的表現與未來成功取決於多項因素，這些因素對我們而言有顯著的機會，但也伴隨風險與挑戰，包括但不限於我們能否從Entropy取得PCC技術授權、潛在供應鏈問題、稅收政策變動及其他支持碳捕獲的激勵措施、我們取得用以資助項目開發所需資金的可及性，以及競爭對手的能源技術可能更早或以更低的成本開發完成。與關鍵設備製造與運輸相關的供應鏈問題，包括因美國或其他國家課徵關稅或其他貿易障礙、措施或衝突所導致，可能導致我們商業化努力的延遲，這可能會影響我們的營運成果、財務狀況與前景。此外，貨幣兌換波動、通貨膨脹、關稅及其他貿易障礙、措施或衝突，可能顯著提高與我們業務相關的運輸費用、原材料成本及其他費用，而這些增加的成本可能對我們的營運成果、財務狀況與前景造成重大且不利的影響。

Net Power正在進行其第一座潔淨穩定發電中心，位於美國德克薩斯州西部的Project Permian場地。此項目規模設計為可容納最高達1吉瓦的潔淨穩定發電容量。我們預計第一階段將使用現有氣渦輪機搭配Entropy的PCC技術。2025年11月12日，我們與買方簽訂協議，購入兩組模組化氣渦輪發電機組，每組的預估總發電量約為30兆瓦，用於Project Permian。第一階段的最終投資決定（"FID"）預計於2026年第三季做出，目標於2029年初開始商業運作，這將使其成為美國首座商業化的潔淨氣體發電項目。
我們是一家開發階段公司，歷史財務結果可能無法反映未來結果，特別是考慮到近期預期氧燃燒循環技術開發時間點的變化，以及潔淨氣體產品的推出。因此，我們未來財務結果的驅動因素，以及這些結果的組成部分，可能與我們歷史或未來營運成果不具可比性。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
自設立以來，我們已產生重大虧損，我們預期未來仍將持續產生虧損，且我們可能無法達成或維持獲利。
我們的電力廠商業可行性取決於客戶願意為潔淨能源支付較高價格，而非未經處理天然氣燃料電力所支付之價格。
我們與合作夥伴可能無法充分控制或準確預測我們專案開發所涉及之成本。
我們可能無法有效管理未來之成長，此無能可能會使執行我們業務策略變得困難。
我們正在開發之專案將依賴複雜機械進行運作，部署過程在運營表現與成本方面涉及相當程度之風險與不確定性。
若我們、合作夥伴或第三方供應商在電力廠關鍵零組件之開發與製造過程中遭遇任何延誤，將可能對我們業務與財務狀況造成不利影響。
我們可能透過合資公司進行淨電力廠之開發，此舉可能導致與合資公司夥伴之間產生爭議，並對我們在合資公司之權益造成不利影響。
零組件原物料之供應不足或成本增加，可能影響廠房設備之製造流程，並提高本公司整體成本。
關鍵設備之製造與運輸可能依賴開放式全球供應鏈。供應鏈問題可能對部署時程產生負面影響。
為準確預測市場需求，本公司可能產生額外成本或遭遇延誤，對本公司業務與財務狀況造成不利影響。
由於董事會中多位董事由主要傳統淨電力持有者及經紀人指定，可能產生利益衝突。
儘管已實施並維護產業標準之安全措施與控制程序，本公司所維護之網站、系統及資料仍可能遭受故意幹擾、其他安全事件或被指控
違反資料處理相關法律、法規或其他義務，可能導致責任並對本公司聲譽及未來銷售產生不利影響。
本公司已產生且未來可能產生損失，係因長期資產之攜帶價值發生減損。
與本公司市場相關之風險
與政府規範相關的風險
我們必須在興建發電廠前取得相關監管核准與許可，且核准可能被拒絕或延宕。
我們可能在發電廠的設計、製造、監管核准與啟動過程中遭遇重大延宕，這可能會使我們無法及時商業化與部署發電廠，甚至完全無法實現。
我們受環境、健康與安全法規及相關規範（如適用）的約束，包括整治事項，這些可能對我們的業務、營運成果與聲譽產生不利影響。
與氣候變遷相關的過渡風險，包括投資人、監管機構及廣泛公眾對化石燃料觀感的負面轉變，可能對我們產生重大且不利的影響。
取得天然氣的限制，包括其生產與配送，以及興建碳封存設施的能力，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們面臨與激勵措施相關的價格波動風險。
任何潛在的政府激勵措施變更或減少，可能對我們擴張業務的能力產生不利影響。
我們可能無法利用任何未來的聯邦所得稅抵免優惠。
與智慧財產權相關的風險
第三方可能成功挑戰或使我們的權利或使用授權智慧財產權的能力失效。
paragraphs: 下列段落討論了可能對我們業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成重大不利影響的最主要風險因素。
Net Power 過去一直產生顯著虧損，並自成立以來經歷負面現金流，包括截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度淨虧損為 578.6 百萬美元，以及截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度淨虧損為 49.2 百萬美元。我們尚未產生任何重大營業收入，但我們有相當高的固定費用。
費用。我們不預期能產生有意義的營業收入，除非且僅在我們能夠完成第一座商業化廠區部署的條件下，而且我們可能無法在預期的時間表內達成此里程碑，甚至可能無法達成。我們尚未成功商業化我們的產品，且可能永遠無法成功，因此，我們很難預測我們未來的營運結果。我們的虧損可能高於預期，且我們可能無法依照預期的時間表達成獲利，甚至可能無法達成；即使我們達成，我們也可能無法維持或提高獲利能力。

儘管我們預期未來幾年營運費用將較過去幾年減少，這是因為我們 La Porte 示範廠區的測試工作已暫停，且我們的業務重點已轉向 PCC，但我們仍預期營運費用在短時間內將遠高於營業收入。若我們無法在長遠時間內足夠提高營業收入以跟上營運費用的成長，可能會導致我們無法達成或維持獲利或正向現金流。此外，若我們未來的成長與營運表現未能符合投資人或分析師的預期，或我們因投資獲取客戶或擴展業務而產生未來負面現金流或虧損，這可能會對我們的業務與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
我們最近擴大了業務範疇，但我們可能無法以具成本效益的方式成功執行我們擴大的業務策略。若我們因任何原因未能成功執行我們擴大的業務策略，可能會對我們的業務與營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。
為回應近期導致本公司認列減損損失的不利事件，我們已擴大業務範疇，以包含利用更標準的簡單循環與複合循環天然氣渦輪機產生電力，並搭配 PCC 技術，作為捕捉這些渦輪機產生的二氧化碳的方法。若我們無法成功執行我們擴大的業務策略，包括開發其他技術及引起客戶對任何衍生產品的興趣等事項，可能會對我們的業務與營運結果造成不利影響。
